['', '\tThe relationship between humans and automation is at a crossroads. What technology and artificial intelligence can do for humanity is up for contention. Three persepctives on the use of modern technology going forward include but are not limited to: dystopian, utilitarian and progressive. All three bring their own nuance to the question at hand, what is lost when we replace humans with machines?', '', "\tA dystopian would see that technology has taken a dark turn, society is on track to be a place where technology controls every aspect of people's lives. In the bleakest form of this future, humans become mere pawns in a game controlled by the all-encompassing reach of technology. As automation becomes more prevalent, humans find themselves increasingly dependent on machines to carry out tasks and make decisions for them. Losing the analogue aproach, can then dull and or even erase humanities understanding of basic tasks, such as long addition/subtraction, woodworking, essay writing and even basic social interaction. This loss of control and autonomy has created a sense of powerlessness among individuals, as they are at the mercy of the technology that governs their existence", '    ', '\tMoreover, the unchecked advancement of technology in a dystopian society can resulted in a stark division between the haves and have-nots. Those in power wield technology as a tool to oppress and control the masses, further entrenching societal inequalities and exacerbating the already dire conditions faced by the disenfranchised. However, what if technology can maximize humanities output for good in the world?', '    ', '\tA utilitarian perspective would suggest that the modern relationship between man and automation can be seen as overwhelmingly positive. As technology has the potential to greatly improve the efficiency and quality of human life. Automation has revolutionized industries, streamlining processes, reducing costs, and increasing productivity in unprecedented ways. By delegating menial and repetitive tasks to machines, humans are able to focus on more complex and creative endeavors, ultimately leading to a more fulfilling and productive society. In this utilitarian view, the benefits of automation far outweigh any potential drawbacks, as technology has the capacity to enhance human well-being and drive progress. Automation has the potential to address some of the most pressing challenges facing humanity, such as climate change, healthcare, and resource management. By harnessing the power of technology, humans can develop innovative solutions to global problems. Technology can help provide solutions to problems, but what if we can escape our limits? ', '    ', '    In the progressive view of the relationship between man and modern technology, the relationship between man and modern technology is characterized by a dynamic and symbiotic partnership that fosters exploration and innovation. Intelligent machines challenge traditional notions of human capabilities, prompting individuals to redefine their roles and push the boundaries of what is considered possible. As humans collaborate with artificial intelligence, they are propelled towards new frontiers, where creativity, adaptability, and ingenuity are essential for success. This collaboration between humans and machines leads to the emergence of new, unforeseen possibilities, encouraging individuals to break free from conventional limitations and embrace a future filled with endless opportunities for growth and advancement. In this progressive view, technology serves as a catalyst for human potential and societal progress, driving individuals towards a path of continuous learning, transformation, and evolution.', '    ', '    There are several examples of technologies that can push human capabilities to new heights. One such example is the field of artificial intelligence (AI), which enables machines to easily perform complex tasks and learn from data in ways that humans could not easily achieve. AI technologies like machine learning and neural networks have the potential to enhance decision-making, problem-solving, and creative thinking abilities for individuals working in various fields such as healthcare, finance, and research.', '', '\tAnother example is virtual reality (VR) technology, which immerses users in interactive, simulated experiences that can expand human understanding and creativity. VR applications in sectors like education, training, and entertainment provide individuals with opportunities to explore new perspectives, enhance spatial reasoning skills, and develop innovative solutions to real-world challenges. Virtual reality can make any task that much more immerisive, allowing anyone to literally see the problem with their eyes. ', '', '\tFurthermore, advancements in robotics technology, particularly in the development of exoskeletons and prosthetic limbs, have the potential to augment human physical capabilities and redefine the limitations of the human body. By integrating human intelligence with robotic assistance, individuals can achieve feats that were previously thought to be impossible, such as overcoming physical disabilities, navigating challenging environments, and enhancing physical strength and endurance. These examples demonstrate how modern technology can empower individuals to transcend traditional boundaries and unlock their full potential in the pursuit of progress and innovation, at the cost of surrendering human control.This surender is the first step to this potential future. ', '    ', '    In conclusion, the relationship between humans and automation stands at a pivotal moment, with divergent perspectives offering nuanced insights into the implications of technology on humanity. The dystopian view highlights the potential risks of ceding control to technology, leading to a future where society is controlled by machines, humans lose their autonomy, and inequalities are exacerbated. Conversely, the utilitarian perspective emphasizes the positive impact of automation on efficiency, productivity, and quality of life, suggesting that technology can address societal challenges and drive progress. Furthermore, the progressive view presents a dynamic partnership between humans and machines that fosters exploration, innovation, and the emergence of new possibilities. Examples of technologies such as artificial intelligence, virtual reality, and robotics showcase the potential for modern tech to push human capabilities to new heights, augmenting creativity, problem-solving skills, and physical abilities. As we navigate the intersection of humanity and technology, it is essential to consider the ethical implications, societal impacts, and potential for collaboration and advancement in shaping a future where humans and machines coexist harmoniously, unlocking a world of endless opportunities for growth, progress, and positive change.', '    ', '    ', '    ']

['Automation is often heralded as a marker of societal progress, yet it raises the important question of what is forfeited when humans are supplanted by machines. Intelligent machines now play a pivotal role in supplying goods and services, taking over functions once performed by humans. From industrial assembly lines to customer service interactions, the growing ubiquity of automation prompts a critical examination of its implications and impact on our lives.', '', 'The dystopian perspective posits that the displacement of human involvement by machines results in a loss of essential humanity. The erosion of basic courtesies, respect, and genuine interpersonal connections in our daily exchanges is a consequence of relying on intelligent machines for various tasks, potentially leading to a disconnect from fundamental social values. Additionally, the diminishing passion and emotion that come with human interaction may be lost in the transactional nature of relationships with automated systems.', '', 'Conversely, the utilitarian view argues that machines excel at monotonous, repetitive tasks and precise, high-speed functions, surpassing humans in efficiency. This efficiency is believed to contribute to the prosperity and advancement of society, benefiting individuals in the long term. However, this efficiency may come at the cost of the passion and creativity that humans bring to their work.', '', 'The progressive standpoint suggests that the advent of intelligent machines challenges traditional concepts of human potential, pushing both humans and machines towards uncharted possibilities. This perspective recognizes the transformative impact of automation on our understanding of humanity and the evolving relationship between humans and technology.', '', 'My perspective aligns with a balance of the utilitarian and progressive views, acknowledging the potential for automation to enhance productivity and innovation in society while also recognizing the risks of losing essential human qualities and passion in the process. Capturing the unique spark and creativity that comes with human interaction, and finding ways to instill these qualities in automated systems, is crucial in navigating the changing landscape of technology and ensuring that advancements in automation lead to a more fulfilling and enriching society. By preserving the passion and emotion that humans bring to their work while reaping the benefits of automation, we can strive towards a future that leverages the strengths of both humans and machines to create a more harmonious and prosperous society.']

['My personal perspective on this issue is that while automation can lead to increased efficiency and progress, it also raises important questions about the role of humans in society. When we replace humans with machines, we risk losing a sense of connection and empathy in our interactions. Also, the displacement of human workers by machines can have negative economic and social consequences. In analyzing the relationship between my perspective and utilitarian view, I can see that while efficiency and progress are important, we must also cosnider the broader implications of automation on society as a whole.', '', "This perspective is very similar to 'Perspective One' due to the fact that it says the replacement of people by machines is essentially losing part of our own humanity. Expanding further on this idea, it becomes apparent that the increasing reliance on automation can also exacerbate existing inequalities within society. Those who are most vulnerable to job displacement, such as low-skilled workers, may face additional challenges in adapting to a rapidly changing labor market. Furthermore, the concentration of wealth and power in the hands of a few technology companies could further widen the gap between the rich and the poor. As I continue to explore the ethical and societal implications of automation, I am committed to advocating for a more balanced approach that prioritizes both efficiency and human well-being.", '', 'In conclusion, my dual interests in literature and environmental science have shaped my perspective on key issues such as automation and its impact on society. By recognizing the potential benefits and drawbacks of automation, I am able to critically analyze the ethical considerations involved in technological advancement. Through a holistic approach that values human connection, empathy, and social equity, I aim to contribute to a more sustainable and just future. As I continue on my academic journey, I am excited to further explore the intersection of these diverse fields and work towards creating a positive impact in the world around me.']

['Automation is often celebrated as a symbol of advancement and efficiency in modern society, yet the implications of replacing humans with machines raise questions about what might be lost in the process. While intelligent machines continue to reshape various industries, there is a growing concern regarding their impact on human capabilities and societal relationships.', '', 'In examining the issue of automation and the displacement of humans by machines, I firmly believe that the current state of intelligent machines, particularly AI, falls short in terms of reasoning and understanding as humans do. The advent of generative AI, such as chatGPT, raises concerns about hindering the growth and potential of the younger generation. The reliance on and interaction with artificial entities may limit human creativity, critical thinking, and emotional intelligence, essential qualities that define our humanity and shape our future.', '', 'Considering the Progressive view that intelligent machines challenge traditional notions of human capabilities and push both humans and machines towards new possibilities, a juxtaposition arises with my perspective. While I acknowledge the potential for machines to drive innovation and expand boundaries, I emphasize the importance of safeguarding human qualities and experiences. The integration of intelligent machines should not come at the cost of suppressing human creativity and emotional connection, which are fundamental aspects of our existence.', '', 'In conclusion, as we navigate the evolving landscape of automation and artificial intelligence, a delicate balance must be struck between technological progress and preserving human essence. While intelligent machines offer opportunities for innovation and growth, it is vital to ensure that they do not overshadow the unique qualities that make us human. By embracing the possibilities that human-machine collaboration presents while safeguarding the core values and capabilities inherent to humanity, we can pave the way for a future where both humans and machines thrive in harmony, driving towards a more interconnected and empathetic society.']

['Automation: "The use of machines, technology, and software to perform tasks that were previously carried out by humans. In the context of replacing human jobs, automation involves the implementation of systems that can perform tasks more efficiently, accurately, and cost-effectively than humans. This can result in job losses as tasks are automated and the need for human labor decreases." ', 'Automation is a big issue nowadays, as AI is becoming increasingly popular, and models such as ChatGPT are assisting people with a variety of tasks, both personal and professional. These AI large language models are efficient and helpful, at least on the surface level. There are a variety of different perspectives regarding automation, illustrated by the dystopian, utilitarian, and progressive viewpoints of automation. ', 'The dystopian view of automation considers the humanity of automation, arguing that we would lose our humanity by replacing people with machines. The utilitarian view of automation considers how efficient automation is and how helpful that would be in the workplace for humans being extremely precise and high-speed. The progressive view argues that automation is a form of progress, allowing us to challenge our long-standing ideas and beliefs about what humans are or can be, ultimately pushing us towards possible unrealized potential.', "Personally, I can understand many of the arguments both for and against automation.  As a business major in college, I understand the potential business-based benefits that automation offers: reduced costs (because an AI LLM doesn't need to be paid for work it produces, unlike a human... but could this cross over into some ethical implications?), safety (reducing human risks by allowing AI to take over the more dangerous aspects of a job), etc. I also can see the potential drawbacks such as the idea of an AI taking over jobs - this is a real concern for jobs that humans may not necessarily need to do (such as accounting, or copywriting). These concerns are valid and real, for both employees and employers. ", "Honestly, I can't say that I'm necessarily for or against automation. I think there are positives and negatives, both yet to be discovered. I can't align my own views with one view provided in the prompt, however I am going into this new, largely uncharted territory with an open mind. I think we will experience a lot of positives, and some negatives throughout this journey.", "I think that I most closely align with the progressive view, which differs vastly from the dystopian view. I'm not automatically assuming that we will lose all humanity when automation becomes more popular. I think there will be positives and negatives to come. "]

['The usage of artificial intelligence has increased over the years, with programs like ChatGPT and others forming new ways to enhance or even replace human work. I feel like there is a fine line between progress and replacement when it comes to machines in lines of work for real people. To give an example, machines used in factories have progressed industrialization and even improved working conditions for factory workers. On the other hand, if machines were to be in replacement for positions that require human interaction like professional athletes, therapists, teachers or even detectives; I believe it would do more damage than good. There are things that are limited to human abilities and there are things that should be left for machines to do. Machines cannot have human emotions and it would be hard to replicate them. Using machines in situations that deal with morality and empathy would only cause the machine to respond with logic. Nowadays, AI is being used for things that were for human enjoyment like art so that it could be profitable. AI is also used academically which can be both good and bad. The use of AI can be beneficial when it is used as an aid and not as a replacement.', "When comparing my perspective to anothers, I would say that my opinion would fall in between the dystopian view and the utilitarian view. I can see why one would think that replacing people with machines would cause us to lose our humanity. It can be thought of as a sci-fi situation where robots replace humans completely. Although it doesn't seem possible for androids to replace us in the near future, it is also a reoccuring thought that machines will soon replace job positions where humans were once working in. I think that if people see more machines replacing job positions, the workload will become more demanding to keep up with the machine - it'll overwork the human employee. In return, this could lead to people having less respect and tolerance from others as stated in the dystopian view.", 'As for the utilitarian view, I agree with the thought that machines are good at low-skill repetitive jobs. This is why it was beneficial in factories and in mass production. It was able to help speed up the process of creating and selling when there is high demand for the product. I believe that before there were machines to do these tasks, there would be people working in unsafe conditions to make sure that these products were sold as fast as possible. Although, this issue is still prevalent now in sweat shops. Efficiency is important in sales and machines did make the process way more efficient.', "To conclude with, intelligent machines have the potential to replace humans and leave it lasting effects but if we were to consistently regulate our usage with machines as a way to only aid our ideas, then it won't get to the point of replacment. It's important to educate others of the consequences of using AI as well as creating technology that is relied on humans instead of the other way around."]

['Automation is growing in our society as we progress by using different intelligent machines that do not require human actions. While this technological advancement may bring about efficiency and convenience, it also raises concerns about the potential impact on humanity in multiple different perspectives. ', '', 'One of these perspectives is a Dystopian view, unemployement can become an issue if intelligent machinery takes over more tasks. For example, people who do not have a degree have to take more manual jobs, but if machines take over those positions, then they will be out of a job. This could widen the economical gap and work to make society more fragmented. Another issue is being more reliant on machinery and not learning the most basic skills due to machines doing it for the human. It would further spiral into people not interacting with others and simply using machines, meaning less knowledge of public respect and courtesy since they are not use to talking to other people. ', '', 'Another perspective is a Utilitarian view, where it can be seen to focus on increasing efficency for the betterment of society. For example, automation could help with people obtaining food by automating goods that people require, like food processing. The more that can be produced, the more people can obtain it. Using more automation could potentially help with creating a future where goods are produced more efficently and people are happier with obtaining different goods. Increasing our current production can be beneifical for all so that there is no lack of vital resources and more people are able to get the help they require. ', '', "The last perspective that was mentioned is the more Progressive view, where automatation and intelligent machinery could be seen as another way to progress forward into a more prosperous world. If machines replace certain jobs, then people would not have to work long, manual hours to earn a livable wage and they can potentially have better careers. There is most likely be less injuries with machine taking over more dangerous jobs. Machine automation also primarily works on low-skill, repetitive jobs, so most likely it would not be able to replace higher career options that require more imagination. There can be new, unexplored possibilies that haven't been discovered since people could have been too busy working on more manual labor. ", '']

['I believe that humans being replaced by machines for some jobs is amazing because of the fact that it stops humans from getting hurt doing some of the tasks that machines can easily do. To work off of the example about assembly lines being supported by robots now instead of using humans, there were definitely benefits there for humans. For example, robots are designed to perform repetitive tasks at a time with a much better endurance than a human can so replacing the humans with robots stops injuries from repetitive motions such as strains and sprains. Robots can also operate the sharp tools and equipment that humans would normally use in the assembly lines which prevents cuts and scars from humans accidently misusing those tools. Lastly, replacing humans with machines helps prevent the many respiratory issues that occur when working in the assembly lines due to the exposure to dust, fumes, or other airborne particles. Overall, replacing humans with machines in assembly lines and other similar types of jobs that are low-skill, repetitive jobs are the type of jobs that should be automated.', '', 'However, while I agree with the utilitarian view in some aspects, I also agree with the dystopian view in the cases that are appearing a lot today. In recent times, there has been an explosion of using robots to automate jobs like cashiers, waiters, and baristas. I completely disagree with using robots to automate jobs like these because these are jobs that lose their human touch when they are replaced by machines. Although I see the convinence in having automated stations for people to order their drinks or check out their items for themselves, that should not be happening at the expense of valuable entry-level jobs that people need in order to establish themselves in the economy. Similarly, I believe that robots should be used to replace some corporate jobs as well such as software engineering and design oriented jobs because although these chatbots have shown their prowless in writing code and creating art, these types of jobs need a human touch for their products to be successful. No matter how much robots improve, until they can truly think like how humans can, I do not believe that we should let them design anything because one of the greatest gifts that humanity has is our boundless imagination.', '', 'Overall, I believe that my perspective on replacing humans with machines does not align with one single perspective but with a mix between the dystopian and the utilitarian perspectives. I want humans to not get hurt as much from the jobs that place them in highly harmful work environments but I also believe that robots should not replace some jobs that require a human touch. I hope that moving forward, people realize that there are some jobs that can be replaced but not every single job can be replaced by machines.']

["\tAs the development of technology advances, the society we live in becomes more and more automated. With this automation brings both benefits and drawbacks for us in many ways. There is a clear economic advantage through automation, but there may be implications for many aspects of a person's financial, social, and psychological life.", '    The automation of repetitive tasks in the workforce has a few major advantages: efficiency, accuracy, and reduced cost of labor, as well as removing humans from potentially dangerous lives in a factory. Machines that can repeat the exact same task many times quickly, without becoming tired, and always in the exact same way allows for the mass production of goods that was not previously achievable. With the advent of AI this advantage only grows, allowing machines to begin to even do jobs that are not repetitive. This includes making decisions to reduce errors and improve safety and efficiency with regards to the processes of creating goods, rather than simply performing the manual labor. AI even allows humans to interact with machines as though they were human. ', '    While these benefits seem great, there are also drawbacks to adding machines to the workforce. One of the most important drawbacks is the impact on employment. Ever since the first addition of machines to assembly lines the problem of employment has been contentious. When a machine takes a job that is traditionally done by a human, the people who make their living with that job tend to experience displacement. This leads to those individuals having economic insecurity and an increase in unemployment and economic inequality in our society. Another major drawback is the effect on the psyche of those in society. Feelings of isolation and disconnection may be brought about as AI is used more and human interaction is needed less. The loss of the human soul in our daily lives can be very damaging to how we see and interact with the world.', '    This view that I hold is a utilitarian view, weighing the benefits and costs of the introduction of machines into the workforce, and the application of AI to increasing the capacity of machines to perform jobs. While I believe that there is great potential for improved production through the use of AI, in the wrong hands and without deliberate caution, the state of our society could deteriorate very quickly.']

['\tAs human beings, we strive to continue progressing toward a better future. Automation has been at the forefront of this ongoing progress, impacting numerous industries and sectors worldwide. From manufacturing and transportation to healthcare and finance. Automation technology has revolutionized the way we work, live, and play. But at what cost? Are we, as a society, losing our connection to one another? Humans are social beings who thrive on connections and relationships with others. While automation and technology have greatly enhanced our efficiency and productivity, they cannot replace the emotional and psychological benefits that come from human interaction. Machines cannot replace humans.', "    The Utilitarian view that machines are faster and more efficient than humans is not wrong, When it comes to manufacturing, many jobs that involve routine, predictable tasks have been replaced by machines. These include tasks such as assembly line work, material handling, packaging, and quality control. Machines can perform these tasks faster, more accurately, and with fewer errors compared to human workers, leading to increased productivity and cost savings for companies. Being as manufacturing is not a customer facing industry, machines don't have as big of an impact on society. However, in industries such as customer service, where face to face interactions can make or break the potential return of customers, robots have more of an impact on society.", '    On one hand, automation in customer service has led to faster response times, 24/7 availability, and personalized interactions through chatbots, virtual assistants, and self-service portals. This has enhanced the overall customer experience by providing instant support, resolving queries quickly, and offering convenient access to information and services. there are concerns about the loss of human touch and empathy in customer interactions when companies rely too heavily on automated systems. While automation can provide quick and efficient responses, it may lack the emotional intelligence, understanding, and personalization that human agents bring to customer service engagements. To address these challenges, companies must strike a balance between automation and human interaction in their customer service operations. By leveraging automation to handle routine tasks and providing human agents for more complex and sensitive interactions, businesses can deliver a personalized, efficient, and empathetic customer experience that meets the diverse needs of customers while supporting the well-being of the workforce.', '']

["\tMachines. Do they help or hurt us? Throughout time we've strove to accomplish tasks efficiently and effectively. Machines are simply a tool that makes accomplishing tasks easier. There are many arguments for both sides, with some believing that machines have made our lives better and others arguing that they have caused harm to society. However, it is important to consider the ways in which machines have revolutionized industries, improved productivity, and even saved lives. As we continue to develop new technologies and integrate them into our daily lives, it is crucial to carefully consider the implications and consequences of our reliance on machines.", '    The view that machines take away something that is human from us is a bit of an exaggeration. The problem is not within machines themself but in how we use them. Of course if you use a tool the wrong way you are going to get hurt. Machines can hurt us if we use them incorrectly and we stop doing things that are beneficial for us. We need to use machines in a way that lets us keep our humanity and make it better at the same time.', '    \tIt is extremely correct that machines help us complete low-skill, repetitive tasks. It saves us room to work on more complex tasks so we can advance  humanity. While it is undeniable that machines play a crucial role in assisting with low-skill, repetitive tasks, they also provide us with the opportunity to free up time and resources to focus on more complex and intellectually stimulating activities. This advancement in technology not only enhances productivity and efficiency, but also fosters innovation and progress in various fields, ultimately contributing to the betterment of society as a whole.', '        A crucial aspect of machines is their ability to push the boundaries of human capability and understanding. They challenge us to rethink our roles in the world and contemplate the possibilities of the future. By embracing machines, we are venturing into uncharted territories and unveiling endless opportunities that were once unimaginable. They serve as the catalyst for innovation and progress, propelling us towards a future where the fusion of human creativity and technological advancement leads to unprecedented achievements. In this rapidly evolving landscape, machines not only redefine the limits of human potential but empower us to shape a world that transcends our wildest dreams.', '        In conclusion, the debate around the impact of machines is a complex issue. While some argue that it can hurt us, it very well can help us if we use them the right way. We can use them to harness the power of our lives and have us work on more complex and advancing issues. There is more to come from machines in the future and we should lookforward to what that holds. ', '       ']

['\tWhen considering the issue of automation, the main point of contention is the amount of automation that can be implemented without significantly undermining individuals\' lives. Perspectives on this issue are largely determined by what each person considers "significant". Some draw the line at automation decreasing the positions available in an industry (i.e. "robots are taking peoples\' jobs") while others recognize the benefits of automation while maintaining skepticism of artificial intelligence such as ChatGPT. Personally, I recognize that the efficiency automation brings enables the lifestyle that I currently enjoy and do not consider automation in areas where human participation is objectively less efficient to be particulary egregious. Though I recognize the merits of the "Dystopian view" as the logic appears to be sound, my own opinion differs considering my social anxiety. The rise of automation in traditionally human-dependent fields, such as customer service, may benefit those who struggle with communication, despite potential drawbacks for those who do not. In other words, the issue of automation can never be "solved" per se as each individual\'s perspective has merit. Put simply, the line is drawn based on one\'s priorities, my perspective prioritizes my comfort whereas the "dystopian" view prioritizes society\'s communication.']

['The issue of automation and society is becoming an incresingly prevalent issue in the modern day as robotics and AI is becoming more sphisticated. We are now entering a world where automation is able to complete many of the different tasks that humans can, meaning that humans will not have to do them any more. These tasks vary, from the low-skill, mundane tasks like cleaning, file organization, and manufactoring, to high-speed tasks like processing. Automation is potentially one of the most important tools that humans have developed, but could also be a problem that accentuates the inequities that are in our socities. ', 'My stance on automation is that we should take full advantage of it where it can increase the quality of human life/other life, but that it should be heavily regulated so that it does not degrade the quality of life of humanity, especially for those in minorities. What I mean by this is allowing AI and automation to be used for some of the mundane tasks that are not necessarily enriching to the human experience, like cleaning, manufactoring, or data entry; or for tasks that can be accomplished much more quickly by a computer like certain kinds of processing. However, we are seeing a situation where AI is creeping in and starting to replace human creative activities and enriching careers that people deticate their lives to. Things like art, creative writing, programming, and science and gradually being overtaken by AI. Additionally, there are situations where minorities or those in lower income brackets are being impacted by automation getting rid of jobs that they need to survive and thrive. Because of this, we need strong regulation on AI and automation to help ensure that it is actually helping humanity, not increasing equity gaps and removing humans from creative acts and professions. ', "When looking at the different perspectives provided, I think that mine most resembles the utilitarian view, but with some caveats. The utilitarian view maintains that machienes should be allowed to take over lower-paying, repetitive jobs so that humans can be more prosperous and pursue more creative activities. I also agree that this should be the case, but I feel that this view leaves out some very important caveats to make sure that machienes also don't leave people out of jobs entirely and widen equity gaps. "]

['Automation is not a new concept. Humans started trying to automate things many years ago. Because of that desire to automate things, we have continued to advance in our knowledge and skills. With that advancement, we are moving into more uncharted territory. Many have their own perspectives on automation. No perspective is wrong.', '', "The three perspectives noted all stem from the fear that if we continue to automate things, our world will be all robots. Increased efficiency in machines means more reliance on them. With more reliance on machines, comes less human interaction. Think of all the movies that have been made where robots go rogue and take over the human world. The movie that comes to my mind when discussing automation is Wall-E. They rely on machines for everything and essentially have become a lazy society.  In the world of Wall-E everyone is living on a ship in space because we ruined our planet. They all rode around in motorized seats and just continued to eat. The Wall-E world with its animation is frightening. Fingers crossed that we don't end up that way.", '', 'I think my overall my perspective lies more in the Utilitarian and Progressive views. I would love for simple jobs to be made easier. I love being able to order on an app and directly note the changes and substitutions I would like. I feel this makes it more accurate and I am less likely to get tomatoes on my sandwich than if I told a human my order. But I also understand that by placing an order within an app has the potential to replace someones job. It is a balancing act between convenience and the people who previously worked the jobs. We need to think long and hard about the implications of advancements in automation and what that would do to our work force. We already have a fairly high unemployment rate, if we push out more self check outs, that takes away more jobs. Where do those people go to make a living? By cutting jobs, are we also increasing our debt as we are potentially having to give more assistance due to lack of jobs? Not every person is going to be able to go from assisting a customer checking out their groceries to a self check out repairperson.', '', '', "So I think we need to really think long and hard about what we want to automate so that we don't push things so far that we turn into the world of Wall-E. Automation is not bad, if done correctly. But really, what is the correct way? It is a question that I think we will continue to ask as we further advance our methods. I am excited to see where things go as the advances we have made are extremely helpful. But I am not sure I am 100% sold on self-driving cars and trucks just yet."]

['Automation is often viewed as a symbol of progress, but I believe it has progressed too quickly without sufficient consideration for the individuals who will be displaced from their jobs as a result. Alongside this, the rise in automation has led to a disassociation from human interaction, resulting in a lack of patience and compassion in society.', '', 'The most pressing concern surrounding automation is the future of job availability for humans. With the advent of robotic drivers for trucks and other automated systems, many workers will find themselves without jobs and lacking the necessary skills to transition into other fields. The potential for training exists, but many workers may not be interested in jobs involving technology maintenance. The displacement of workers in various industries raises questions about how individuals will sustain themselves financially in the future.', '', 'Furthermore, the erosion of respect in daily interactions is a concerning trend resulting from decreased human contact. As people increasingly turn to online platforms for communication, there is a noticeable decline in empathy and tolerance in face-to-face interactions. This shift towards a more self-centered mentality is exacerbated by the removal of human elements from everyday activities.', '', 'Moreover, the evolution of technology has not progressed as smoothly as anticipated, with frequent system glitches and aggravating processes causing frustration for users. Rather than simplifying tasks, automation has often led to complicated and inefficient experiences for individuals, highlighting the limitations of technology in enhancing daily life.', '', 'While Perspective Three, the idea of progress through automation, may seem promising, it is essential to consider the impact on human integrity and job opportunities. Instead of solely focusing on profitability and technological advancement, we should prioritize creating innovations that genuinely improve lives and generate employment for individuals.', '', 'In conclusion, it is crucial for society to pause and reflect on the current state of automation, envision where we aim to be in the future, and identify gaps in achieving these objectives. By taking a step back and reassessing our approach to automation, we can ensure a future that instills hope rather than anxiety among individuals.', '', '']

['With the rise of intelligent machines and automation in the workplace, there are both advantages and disadvantages that need to be considered. As a society, it is crucial for us to carefully weigh the positive and negative impacts of increasing automation in order to move forward in a way that maximizes benefits and minimizes drawbacks. There are three main perspectives on intelligent machines in the workplace: the dystopian perspective, the utilitarian perspective, and the progressive perspective.', '', 'The dystopian perspective posits that our society may lose some of its humanity by becoming overly reliant on machines in the workplace. This viewpoint highlights the potential loss of interpersonal connections, empathy, and the sense of community that can result from a decrease in human interaction in the workplace. On the other hand, the utilitarian perspective argues that machines are best suited for handling low-skill, repetitive tasks that require high levels of precision. This efficiency can lead to increased productivity and overall benefit for humanity. Lastly, the progressive perspective suggests that machine intelligence challenges our traditional notions of humanity, opening up new possibilities and pushing both humans and machines towards unexplored potential.', '', 'Personally, I find myself leaning towards a combination of the dystopian and utilitarian perspectives on machine intelligence in the workplace. While I recognize the benefits that automation and machines can bring by streamlining repetitive tasks and increasing worker productivity, I am also wary of the potential consequences, such as mass unemployment and the exacerbation of wealth inequality between different socioeconomic classes. It is important for us as a society to carefully navigate the integration of intelligent machines in the workplace in order to ensure a balance between efficiency and human well-being. By finding this balance, we can harness the benefits of automation while also mitigating its negative impacts on the workforce and society as a whole.']

['When considering the issue of what is lost when we replace humans with machines, it is important to further define the issue. Humans being replaced by machines could mean a variety of things. Therefore, I will clarify that in this paper, when the topic of humans being replaced with machines is mentioned, it is referring to the idea of automated AI systems handling tasks that are repetitive and do not require any kind of human decision-making. In this context, I would consider that nothing is actually lost in this process as long as the tasks being automated are indeed repetitive and free from the need for any kind of decision-making.', '', 'Instead of focusing on the idea that the machine is now doing a job a human once held, it should be recognized that the human who previously held this position will now be able to enhance the effectiveness of their work by finding employment that is more meaningful instead of redundant, mindless work. This will not only improve the production of most industries but also provide the individual with the opportunity to make a better contribution to their company and society. In turn, this will help counteract the negative effects that their previous type of work had on their mental health. Considering a dystopian point of view on this topic, if someone with this type of thinking were to voice their view, they would probably argue that automation strips humans of their purpose and reduces the value of human labor to mere survival, leaving people without meaningful work. They might suggest that such a shift could lead to widespread unemployment, social unrest, and a loss of personal identity for those who derive a sense of purpose from their work. Such a viewpoint would highlight concerns about increased inequality, where the benefits of automation are concentrated in the hands of those who own the machines, while the displaced workers are left without a clear path forward. This could foster resentment and lead to societal divisions, with the potential for significant social upheaval if a large segment of the population feels left behind by technological progress.', '', 'However, this perspective is often contrasted with more optimistic views that emphasize the potential for humans to adapt and find new, more fulfilling roles in an automated world. The key argument against the dystopian view is that throughout history, technological advances have consistently led to the creation of new industries and jobs that were previously unimaginable. For example, the Industrial Revolution, while initially displacing many manual laborers, eventually led to the creation of entirely new fields of work, improved standards of living, and greater overall societal wealth. In this optimistic view, automation could be seen as an opportunity to reimagine work and redefine what it means to have a fulfilling career. As machines take over the drudgery of repetitive tasks, humans can focus on what makes them uniquely human—creativity, empathy, innovation, and complex problem-solving. The challenge, then, is not to resist automation, but to manage its implementation in a way that ensures the benefits are broadly shared and that workers are supported in transitioning to new roles. Ultimately, the discussion around humans being replaced by machines in repetitive tasks is not just about the efficiency and productivity gains but also about how society chooses to handle the transition and what new opportunities can be created in the wake of these changes.', '']

['When automation reaches the point where vast numbers of human workers are replaced by machines, the fabric of society begins to unravel. In this light, I do not perceive the replacement of most human roles as progress; true progress, in my view, is one that improves the lives of a vast majority of humanity.', '', 'For instance, automation of mindless tasks can indeed be beneficial. The replacement of such positions is remarkable, especially considering the current state of the world where humans should not be laboring as slaves for minimal wages or in hazardous conditions that put their lives at risk. Particularly in industries like mining and natural resource harvesting (e.g., lithium mining for batteries, coal for power plants, logging for timber), replacing humans with machines is not only ideal but imperative. In my personal opinion, the loss of income pales in comparison to the loss of life.', '', 'On the other hand, the AI-generated art in the creative sectors is a notion that I find regressive. The lack of creativity and attention to detail in AI-generated art is stark, as machines lack the capability to truly understand the essence of creativity. AI art is a soulless product devoid of the emotion and meaning that are intrinsic to human-created art. An artist, with their unique perspective and emotions, can produce abstract art that resonates on a deeper level.', '', 'Continuing down the path where almost every human role is superseded by machines will inevitably dismantle the very fabric of our society. In a capitalist society like ours where earned income is the foundation of life, the scenario where 99% of people are devoid of income while the remaining 1% control the machines spells disaster. Society will crumble, leading to starvation, conflicts over resources, and a breakdown of knowledge. Such a world, dominated by machines with a minority controlling them, would mark the end of the world as we know it.', '', "In evaluating the various perspectives on the replacement of human workers with machines, it becomes evident that each viewpoint brings forth unique concerns and advantages. While my standpoint underscores the potential societal and cultural implications of extensive automation, emphasizing the significance of human interaction, creativity, and economic stability, the utilitarian perspective recognizes the efficiency and progress that automation can bring, particularly in tasks where machines excel over humans. Conversely, the progressive viewpoint envisions the untapped possibilities that intelligent machines can offer, challenging traditional notions about human potential. While my perspective advocates for the preservation of human connections and the essence of creativity, the utilitarian and progressive viewpoints acknowledge the advancements and opportunities that automation can offer in terms of productivity and technological innovation. Exploring the interplay of these contrasting perspectives sheds light on the complex and nuanced nature of the discourse surrounding automation's impact on society.", '', 'The ongoing debate surrounding the replacement of human workers with machines encompasses a myriad of complexities and nuances, reflecting diverse perspectives on the societal, economic, and cultural implications of automation. While valid concerns exist regarding the potential loss of human connections and creativity, it is crucial not to overlook the efficiencies and progress facilitated by automation. As we navigate this evolving landscape, striking a delicate balance between technological advancements and the preservation of essential human traits becomes paramount to ensure a sustainable and inclusive future for all.']

['Automation of machinery has led to immense advancements not only in efficiency but also in the quality of products, from farming equipment to automating driving and flying. It is clear that automation is a beneficial factor in the world. In my opinion, automation is one of the key cornerstones of our current world.', '', "First of all, automation is a beneficial advancement for the world as it enables tasks to be completed faster and more efficiently. One notable example is in the manufacturing industry, where automated machinery allows for the production of more goods at a quicker rate and often of higher quality. With the global population continuously increasing, automated machinery plays a crucial role in meeting the needs of people. For instance, in the agricultural sector, automated farming equipment is vital in ensuring food security as manual farming methods are inefficient and insufficient to feed the world's population.", '', 'On the other hand, excessive automation can lead to a lack of humanity and result in individuals losing their jobs and sources of income. For example, the widespread implementation of self-checkout machines and other automated processes has led to the displacement of jobs previously held by humans. While automation may enhance efficiency from a consumer standpoint, it diminishes the personal interaction and human touch provided by a human cashier. This loss of connection and personal touch in daily interactions is a concerning aspect of increased automation. Furthermore, for employees whose livelihoods depend on these jobs, automation can be perceived as a negative force, potentially leading to financial instability and a sense of loss or purpose.', '', 'Considering both perspectives, I believe that automation plays a significant role in progressing both the world and humanity. As mentioned in my first point, automation enables us to meet the needs of a growing population and enhance the production of goods. However, it is essential to acknowledge that excessive automation can potentially erode the human element, leading to a loss of personal connections and interactions that are vital for societal cohesion. Regarding the issue of unemployment raised in my second point, I maintain my perspective on automation. I do not view automation as a problem, as it has the potential to free up human resources and time, allowing us to focus on different goals and pursuits. For example, if everyone had to engage in manual labor just to meet basic needs, we would not have the opportunity to advance in other areas such as technology, science, and innovation. Automation provides us with the time and resources to explore, create, and imagine new inventions, goods, and solutions that can further benefit the world.', '', 'In conclusion, while acknowledging the concerns surrounding automation, it is important to recognize its significant benefits. Automation enhances efficiency, productivity, and innovation, enabling us to meet the needs of a growing population and focus on higher-level pursuits. By embracing automation as a tool for empowerment and advancement, we can drive progress, explore new frontiers, and create solutions to complex challenges. Finding a balance between the benefits of automation and the preservation of human values is key to navigating this technological shift successfully. Ultimately, automation has the potential to propel society forward and shape a future where technology and humanity can coexist harmoniously.', '', '']

", 'There is probably some credence to the idea of the dystopian view, then, when we consider the points above. There is more than enough evidence to debunk the second, more utilitarian, view. ['\tI think that automation has both pros and cons. However, allowing machines to take over so many aspects of our lives can also lead to a regression in the overall social capabilities of humans. For example, many people will order food through an app or website, avoiding the social interaction associated with ordering food. While this is very convenient, it also leads to many people feeling anxious when ordering in person. ', '', '\tMy view is a combination of the utilitarian and dystopian views.
